title: Off-Plan Runs on Believers: Who Creates Them and What Happens When They Leave
seoTitle: Off-Plan Runs on Believers. Here Is How It Breaks.
description: Off-plan markets are fuelled by belief. The three players who create believers, why Miami and Dubai are full of them, and what Toronto shows when they leave.
answer: Off-plan markets run on belief. A tower gets built only when enough buyers believe a unit will be worth more later. Three players create those believers: the visionary developer, the brand that lends its name, and the early investors. When they step back, sales can fall almost to zero, as Toronto showed this summer with 60 presale sales in three months.
body:
Toronto sold almost 31,000 new condos in 2021. This summer, in three months, it sold 60. The cranes are still there and the money did not leave the city. What left were the believers.

## Belief is the fuel of off-plan

Nobody buys a drawing unless they believe in what it will become. A tower only goes up when enough people with money believe the unit will be worth more later than it costs today. Right now, two markets are full of that belief. At the start of 2026, Miami had about 150 condo projects in pre-construction across downtown, Miami Beach and Broward, with close to 18,000 units on the way. In Dubai, about three out of four homes sold in the first half of the year were off-plan.

## The three players who create believers

- **The visionary.** The developer who looks at a parking lot and sees a tower.
- **The brand.** A hotel, fashion or car name placed next to the developer.
- **The deep pockets.** The investors who commit before anyone else.

When the three move together, a city grows. Each one feeds the others: the brand makes the vision easier to believe, and early money makes the brand comfortable. Every buyer who joins later is following that signal.

## What happens when belief runs out

In Toronto, investors were the majority of presale buyers. When higher rates meant rents no longer covered mortgages, they stopped buying. Sales fell, and soon after, new construction slowed to its lowest level since early 2012. That is the part people miss: the believers do not leave alone. The cranes leave with them.

This is not a crash forecast for Miami or Dubai. It is a reminder, in my opinion, of what to watch: not the cranes, the believers.

The full episode covers the nightclub line, the Toronto numbers and five warning signs. Listen at [/podcast/off-plan-runs-on-believers-here-is-how-it-breaks/](/podcast/off-plan-runs-on-believers-here-is-how-it-breaks/).
takeaways: Off-plan sales depend on buyers believing a unit will be worth more later.
The visionary, the brand and the deep pockets create that belief together.
Miami and Dubai are currently full of off-plan believers.
When believers leave, construction slows as well as sales.
faq: What drives off-plan real estate demand?
Belief that the unit will be worth more at completion than at purchase. Without enough buyers who share that belief, projects do not launch.
Who creates demand for a new development?
The developer with the vision, a brand that adds its name, and early investors who commit first. Together they create the momentum other buyers follow.
How much of Dubai is sold off-plan?
As reported for the first half of 2026, about three out of four homes sold in Dubai were off-plan.
